hypotheses.statement: Across all held-out signal trials, the DRR-Mellin scan recovers the hidden log-frequency more often than each of Lomb-Scargle, periodogram-initialized NLS and ESPRIT.

hypotheses.decision: one-sided z test of the difference between the two mean paired differences (independent trials); supported if p < 0.05
hypotheses.statement: Under additive noise (white and Student-t), the DRR-Mellin recovery advantage over Lomb-Scargle is larger for strongly growing or decaying modes (|beta| = 0.6) than for constant-amplitude modes (beta = 0).

hypotheses.decision: supported if the one-sided 95% lower confidence bound of the mean paired difference (DRR minus Lomb-Scargle) exceeds -0.03
hypotheses.statement: At beta = 0, where Lomb-Scargle is the matched statistic, searching over growth costs the DRR-Mellin scan at most 3 percentage points of recovery.

drr_log_spectrum.description: drr_framework.mellin.log_spectrum with its documented beta = 0.5 weighting on a uniform ln-x grid (linear interpolation when samples are not log-uniform); statistic peak / mean power in the search band

drr_mellin_scan.description: drr_framework.mellin.log_mode_profile on the raw samples: joint least-squares scan over 17 growth exponents and 581 log-frequencies; statistic 1 - relative SSE

esprit.description: least-squares ESPRIT, model order 2, Hankel depth n // 3, on a uniform ln-x grid (linear interpolation when samples are not log-uniform); statistic energy fraction of the two leading singular values

lomb_scargle.description: scipy.signal.lombscargle of the mean-removed samples against ln x on the same frequency grid; statistic 2 x peak power / total sum of squares

nls.description: scipy.optimize.least_squares fit of exp(beta u)(a cos omega u + b sin omega u), u = centred ln x, started at the Lomb-Scargle peak with beta = 0; statistic 1 - relative SSE
